title: When a metabolizing enzyme variant matters

segs.text: Section eight. When a metabolizing enzyme variant matters. She said, Variations in our metabolizing enzymes are the biggest reason why we would see variation in drug response. A variant becomes clinically important in three cases. The enzyme is the major route that eliminates the drug or ends its action. The drug is a prodrug that needs activation. Or an altered pathway, or the parent drug itself, causes toxicity.

The direction of harm depends on whether the drug is already active or is a prodrug. A poor metabolizer cannot run the enzyme step. So an active drug is not removed and climbs toward toxicity, while a prodrug is never turned on and fails. An ultrarapid metabolizer runs the step too fast. So an active drug is gone before it works, and a prodrug is over activated, which can overdose the patient.

Clopidogrel shows that the busiest enzyme is not always the one that decides the outcome. It is a prodrug. About eighty five percent of a dose is inactivated by esterases, and only about fifteen percent is activated in two C Y P steps. Variants in C Y P two C nineteen most change how much active drug forms.
